criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Real images, not headlines over objects. Frame 3's directive card sits at a rake with a curling corner and is the one frame a reader would screenshot. Frame 9's tower runs off the top edge with a figure at its base giving true scale. But three frames solve type the same way and solve it with a plate: on 2, 6 and 8 the headline sits inside a darkened rectangle whose edge is visible at 432px. Frame 5 is slabs in a void and its repaired casts collapse into a single diagonal hatch band at feed size, so the repair does not reach a reader.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: One light runs the whole deck and every cast falls right. One halftone cell, one ground, one cream, cyan reserved for water alone. Two continuity devices genuinely work at thumb size. What holds it under 7 is adjacency: two hard cuts in eight steps and neither is where the argument turns. Worse for a reader, the trough sits on 5 and 6, the two frames carrying who asks whom and why it matters, while the peak sits on 2, a threshold number. The value is loudest where the deck has least to say.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: I tried to refute this and could not. Every numeral on every frame traces, and the caption's likewise. The eight rejections are honoured in the copy and not just in the claims file. Frame 3 reproduces c6 and c7 verbatim under the source's own masthead, so the reader sees the attribution rather than being asked to trust it. The one softening is frame 9's 'expected in December' where c19 reads 'no later than December 10, 2026', and the frame prints December 10th directly beneath it, so a reader gets both.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: It does tell a Texan something they did not know, and frame 3 lands it. What it does not do is put the subject where a reader can reach it. THE WORDS 'DATA CENTER' AND 'WATER' APPEAR IN NO HEADLINE ON ANY OF THE NINE FRAMES. They live only in deks and kickers, which render at 9.6 to 13px in the feed. The stake sits on frame 6, the deck's flattest frame, in its smallest type. Nothing in nine frames says what the state water plan decides for a person in a drought.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: 1 to 2 to 3 builds and 3 is the genuine turn. Then frame 4 is where I stop, confirming the round 4 finding that went unactioned. Frame 9's new headline does break the third X-is-due-on-DATE construction and is a real partial fix, and 7 and 8 are still back to back in the same layout with their dates running backwards, so a reader swiping a date spine reads 14, 12, December.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: House rules hold everywhere I checked, and the caption's comma density is very low with the only writer-chosen commas inside a verbatim quote. But there is no Texan in the voice, only in the wordmark and the word Texas on frame 1. This is a well-edited wire desk, which is flat, and flat is the operative word when the deck already carries no place.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: Third data center deck in six days and the second ERCOT request carrying a notarized attestation in five. SELECTION.md names the adjacency and argues the separations honestly, and they are real, which is why this is not a hard fail. But the topics ledger has recorded this same instrument blind spot in capitals on six decks and nothing reads the field. Second charge: SELECTION lists Pivot as SPENT, names Clock as the natural structure, and the shipped caption structure is Pivot, on a stale exclusion menu.

walks_away_with: In Texas, not returning your water use survey was already a crime, and the state just started enforcing it.
would_stop_scrolling_at: frame 4, the same answer as round 4, because nothing changed there.
on_naming_the_institutions: NOT enough, and it needed to be on the cover. Frame 5 does the mapping work well and that dek renders at roughly 11px in a 432px feed and its labels at roughly 8px. A phone reader does not read it, and frame 2 says 'The survey is the board's' three frames before 'the board' has any antecedent. The fix was right in kind and landed in the wrong type layer.
next_run_fix: Rewrite the cover headline so it carries the subject. 'Texas already had the power to ask' never says who asked, whom, or about what, and it is the one frame most readers will ever see.
one_sentence_fix: Put the subject nouns in the headline layer, starting with the cover, because at 432px the nine headlines are the only type a feed reader receives and not one of them contains the words 'data center' or 'water'.
